# Voice and tone

How PLUS sounds to everyone it serves.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ContentVoiceAndTone.mdx`

## Voice

Our voice is helpful, honest, warm and clear. Who we are stays the same; how we say it fits who is reading.

| Word | The idea | What it asks of the writer |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | The purpose · Productivity | Point to the next step. Tell people what is coming, then show them how to get there. |
|  | The truth · Learning | Say what happened. Give feedback straight, with the reason. Own our mistakes. |
|  | The feeling · Uplift | Write the way a colleague talks. Notice the effort. Skip the jargon. |
|  | The words · Simplicity | Keep it short. Use everyday words. Lead with the verb. One idea per sentence. |

## When to dial

The four words never change. How hard we lean on each one does.

| Word | Lean in | Pull back |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | A tutor is about to start a session. | The reader is browsing, not doing. |
|  | Something failed, or a student is stuck. | Never. Soften how you say it, not what you say. |
|  | A student did well. A tutor showed up. | Money, policy, or an error. |
|  | A live session, a phone, a hurry. | Never. Clear is always on. |

### Warm, pulled back

When money is late, warm means calm and specific. The date is the kindest part.

Do: Kind, because it answers “when?”.
Don't: Polite, but the tutor still has to ask when.

## Tone

One moment, told five ways: Maya, a sixth-grade student, can now solve fractions on her own. However the tone shifts, it always sounds like PLUS.

| Reader | Where | Tone | The line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tutor | Product | Quick, warm, like a teammate | “Maya solved her first fraction on her own. Nice work this week.” |
| Supervisor | Product | Brief, factual, ranked | “Maya mastered fractions in four sessions with her tutor, Priya.” |
| Researcher | Product | Precise, neutral, numbers first | “Fractions: mastered at session 4. School B, grade 6.” |
| Teacher | Service | Respectful, free of product terms | “Maya can now solve fractions on her own. Next, her tutor moves on to decimals.” |
| Student | Service | Short, kind, about effort | “You did it, Maya. Fractions are yours.” |

## In the product

One card for each person who uses PLUS. The voice holds; the tone shifts with the job. In each card the headline is the action, what to do next, and the body says why it matters in that reader’s terms.

| Reader | Context | Headline (the action) | Body (why it matters) | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tutor | Today · 3:30 PM · Breakout room 3 · Starts in 10 min | Prep for Maya’s session | Last week you tagged her Stuck on fractions. Start with a warm-up problem to build her confidence. | Open session · View notes |
| Lead tutor | Room 3 · Attendance · 2 of 6 joined | Mark attendance for Room 3 | Four students haven’t joined yet. Marking them absent frees their tutors for students who are here. | Mark attendance · Wait 5 min |
| Supervisor | Reviews · This week · 2 urgent | Start with 2 urgent reflections | Priya flagged a session where a student seemed upset. Reading it first lets you check in before her next session. | Open review · See all 5 |
| Researcher | Exports · Fall term · Ready | Your export is ready | 1,240 sessions from three schools, with student names removed. It matches the filters you saved on Monday. | Download CSV · Edit filters |
